reference: GNU coreutils 9.7 cat, invoked by system Bash on the reference side; stderr is compared byte for byte after the shell's script-line prefix is removed.
coverage: Guest compatibility pass 6 (G90): GNU diagnostic wording for operand and usage errors.
exclusions: Only diagnostics are covered here; the reviewed suite in suites/ covers ordinary operation.

cases.purpose: G90: a read error names the operand as GNU does ('cat: d: Is a directory', '-' for standard input), and an open error keeps the bare name. The shell's script-line prefix is stripped so the case holds before and after the builtin-prefix change.
cases.script:
mkdir d
printf 'kept\n' > f
{ cat d || echo rc=$?; } 2>err
{ cat < d || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
{ cat nosuch f || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //' err >&2
rm err

cases.purpose: Docker parity errors/cat: glibc getopt wording plus the coreutils Try line for an unknown long option, an unknown option letter inside a cluster, an argument given to a flag, and an ambiguous abbreviation (listed in GNU order); a unique abbreviation is accepted.
cases.script:
cat --bogus </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
cat -n@ </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
cat --number=3 </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
cat --num </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
cat a --bogus </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"
printf 'x\ty\n' | cat --show-t </dev/null || echo "rc=$?"

cases.purpose: Docker parity files/cat-e-crlf: -E shows the CR of a CRLF line end as ^M (GNU 9.x), keeps other CRs, and carries a CR at the end of one file over to the next.
